macros.name: backgroundpath
macros.doc: This command specifies the path that “makes up” the background of the shape.

macros.name: beforebackgroundpath
macros.doc: This command works like \behindbackgroundpath, only the ⟨code⟩ is executed after the background path has been used, but before the texts label are drawn.

macros.name: behindforegroundpath
macros.doc: The ⟨code⟩ is executed after the text labels have been drawn, but before the foreground path is used.

macros.name: deferredanchor
macros.doc: This command declares an anchor named ⟨name⟩.

macros.name: foregroundpath
macros.doc: This command works like \backgroundpath, only it is invoked after the text labels have been drawn.

macros.name: inheritanchor
macros.doc: Inherits the code of one specific anchor named ⟨name⟩ from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritanchorborder
macros.doc: Inherits the border anchor code from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritbackgroundpath
macros.doc: Inherits the background path code from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritbeforebackgroundpath
macros.doc: Inherits the before background path code from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritbeforeforegroundpath
macros.doc: Inherits the before foreground path code from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritbehindbackgroundpath
macros.doc: This command can be used to inherit the code used for the drawings behind the background path from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritbehindforegroundpath
macros.doc: Inherits the behind foreground path code from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritforegroundpath
macros.doc: Inherits the foreground path code from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: inheritsavedanchors
macros.doc: This command allows you to inherit the code for saved anchors from ⟨another shape name⟩.

macros.name: nodeparts
macros.doc: This command declares which parts make up nodes of this shape.

macros.name: pgfcoordinate
macros.doc: This command creates a node of shape coordinate at the given ⟨coordinate⟩.

macros.name: pgfdeclareplothandler
macros.doc: This command creates a new plot handler that can subsequently be called using the macro ⟨macro⟩.

macros.name: pgfdeclareshape
macros.doc: This command declares a new shape named ⟨shape name⟩.

macros.name: pgfmultipartnode
macros.doc: This command is the more general (and less user-friendly) version of the \pgfnode command. While the \pgfnode command can only be used for shapes that have a single part (which is the case for most shapes), this command can also be used with multi-part nodes.

macros.name: pgfnode
macros.doc: This command creates a new node.

macros.name: pgfnodealias
macros.doc: This command does not actually create a new node. Rather, it allows you to subsequently access the node ⟨existing node⟩ using the name ⟨new name⟩.

macros.name: pgfnodepostsetupcode
macros.doc: When you call this macro inside a scope for which the \pgfpositionnodelater has been called, the ⟨code⟩ will be stored internally. Later, when the node named ⟨node name⟩ is actually positioned using \pgfpositionnodenow, the ⟨code⟩ will be executed.

macros.name: pgfnoderename
macros.doc: This command renames an existing node.

macros.name: pgfplotfunction
macros.doc: This command will produce coordinates by iterating the ⟨variable⟩ over all values in ⟨sample list⟩, which should be a list in the \foreach syntax.

macros.name: pgfplotgnuplot
macros.doc: This command will “try” to call the gnuplot program to generate the coordinates of the ⟨function⟩.

macros.name: pgfplothandlerdiscard
macros.doc: This handler will simply throw away the stream.

macros.name: pgfplothandlerlineto
macros.doc: This handler will issue a \pgfpathlineto command for each point of the plot, except possibly for the first.

macros.name: pgfplothandlerpolygon
macros.doc: This handler works like the line-to plot handler, only the line is closed at the end using \pgfpathclose, resulting in a polygon.

macros.name: pgfplothandlerrecord
macros.doc: When this handler is installed, each time a plot stream command is called, this command will be appended to ⟨macro⟩. Thus, at the end of the stream, ⟨macro⟩ will contain all the commands that were issued on the stream.

macros.name: pgfplotstreamend
macros.doc: This command signals that a plot stream ends.

macros.name: pgfplotstreamnewdataset
macros.doc: This command indicated that in the stream a “new data set” starts.

macros.name: pgfplotstreampointundefined
macros.doc: This command indicated that the stream contains an “undefined” point like a point where some coordinate results for a division by zero.

macros.name: pgfplotstreamspecial
macros.doc: This command causes \pgf@plotstreamspecial to be called with ⟨text⟩ as its parameter.

macros.name: pgfplotstreamstart
macros.doc: This command signals that a plot stream starts.

macros.name: pgfplotxyzfile
macros.doc: This command works like \pgfplotxyfile, only three numbers are expected on each non-empty line.

macros.name: pgfpointanchor
macros.doc: It returns the coordinate of the given ⟨anchor⟩ in the given ⟨node⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointshapeborder
macros.doc: This command returns the point on the border of the shape that lies on a straight line from the center of the node to ⟨point⟩.

macros.name: pgfpositionnodenow
macros.doc: This command is used to position a node that has previously been created using the command \pgfpositionnodelater.

macros.name: pgfsetlinetofirstplotpoint
macros.doc: Specifies that plot handlers should issue a line-to command for the first point of the plot.

macros.name: pgfsetmovetofirstplotpoint
macros.doc: Specifies that the line-to plot handler (and also some other plot handlers) should issue a move-to command for the first point of the plot instead of a line-to.

macros.name: savedanchor
macros.doc: This command declares a saved anchor.

macros.name: usepgfmodule
macros.doc: Once the core has been loaded, you can use this command to load further modules.
